speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Research Foundation (NRF) seeks to build a thriving Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) ecosystem that drives an innovation economy and addresses Singapore’s national imperatives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, our RIE investments have benefited Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Investments in biomedical sciences and medical technology since the 1990s have set the foundation for the flourishing sectors they are today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As of 2020, Singapore hosts more than 30 regional headquarters (HQs) in the sector, many of which are from the world’s top pharmaceutical and med-tech firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will support the next bound of Singapore’s economic transformation by advancing Singapore’s capabilities in strategic technology areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will unlock new opportunities for growth and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, in the area of semiconductors, our public research institutes and universities are collaborating with industry through corporate laboratories and joint projects, to work on new materials, designs, and manufacturing techniques that can drive the next generation of more efficient and powerful chips.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These innovations will enable advances in wide-ranging applications such as wearables, communications equipment and vehicles, and expand the base of semiconductor manufacturing activities and jobs in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is another technology with transformative potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to attract top AI talent and spur the development of innovative AI solutions that generate value for businesses and society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to support transformation efforts of businesses across industry sectors by creating new and improved solutions that leverage science and technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are scaling up platforms that bring together our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), public research institutes and industry, so that technological advancements in areas, such as medical diagnostics and additive manufacturing, are more quickly commercialised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies can also establish corporate laboratories with our public research performers to address their industry challenges or tap on Centres of Innovation for technical and business advisory to support their journey to become product builders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many large corporations and multinationals have anchored their R&D centres in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Small-Medium Enterprises are also growing their innovation ambition and capabilities by tapping on capabilities in the IHLs and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), and on platforms, such as the Global Innovation Alliance, which provide access to enterprise partners, talent and markets in international innovation hubs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the next phase, as part of the Singapore Global Enterprises Initiative to build more locally-grown, high-growth and globally competitive companies, we will provide customised financial support for promising enterprises to build sustained R&D and innovation capacity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to its economic importance, RIE has been critical in addressing Singapore’s challenges in areas, such as public health and resource resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our R&D capabilities in biomedical sciences and infectious diseases enabled us to respond to COVID-19 quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore was one of the first countries to successfully culture the SARS-CoV-2 virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also developed several diagnostic test-kits that were rapidly deployed for use both locally and overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our early investments to diversify our water sources, such as creating and adapting technologies for NEWater and desalination, have also helped make our water supply more secure and resilient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to invest in R&D to tackle ongoing and future challenges, for instance, to improve our pandemic preparedness by bolstering our vaccine development capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To respond to the existential threat of climate change, we are deepening our investments in low carbon energy research and strengthening our climate adaptation R&D efforts, including by investing in coastal protection and flood management research.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are investing in food R&D particularly in aquaculture, urban agriculture, alternative proteins, and food safety, to strengthen our food security while reaping economic benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A robust talent pool is a key enabler for good RIE investment outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to build a strong core of local research talent by nurturing our youths’ interest in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) fields, and providing diverse pathways for those who wish to take up research careers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our RIE investments have created a strong foundation for Singapore to remain competitive amidst rapid technological changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to leverage and build Singapore’s science and technology capabilities to meet imminent needs and challenges, capture new economic opportunities and support our businesses and workforce.
